uncertainFacts: Island ROW ORDER is set by boss level, not by any single source's list order. Sportskeeda's numbered list is not strictly level-sorted (e.g. it lists Raven Ridge L90 after a L100 boss), so level is used as the canonical sort key.
Spelling 'Lava Crag' is used (majority: Sportskeeda, Pro Game Guides, Nerdschalk, Destructoid). evomon.site spells it 'Lava Crack'; treated as a minority typo and not used.
'Summon Ruins' is excluded by parent decision: sources describe it as a boss-summoning hub, not a numbered progression island.

'Flying Territory' is a DESCRIPTIVE label, not a confirmed in-game zone name. Sources say its boss 'King of Flying' / Sundercrene is obtained there as a flying mount. In-game zone name must be verified before publish; rename or drop if it is not a real zone.

Islands and bosses past #5 (Shiver Snows) are flagged by Nerdschalk as not fully community-verified in writing. Boss names for Raven Ridge (Viparch is Murkwood, etc.) are second-source corroborated via search, but exact BOSS LEVELS for islands 6-14 come only from Sportskeeda and are marked sourceConfidence 'low'.
Dominant-type per island is well-documented only for islands 1-5. Later islands' dominant types are not reliably sourced and are left null rather than guessed.
Notable Evomon per island is only sparsely sourced; left null where no source names a specific catch.
No clean per-island image source was found. All image fields are null; images are owned by the image gate (likely in-game screenshots).
meta.imageAcceptedMissingReason: No clean per-island zone thumbnail or reliably mappable island-boss render exists from a reusable source. Dedicated map pages (evomon.org/map/island-order, bo3.gg) return 403/empty; dex wikis (evomon.app/dex, evomon.net/wiki, evomon.wiki/dex) are JS-driven catalogs of standard creature art and do not expose King/boss-variant renders. Per parent guidance, accepted text-first rather than using bad/unrelated images.

items.name: Verdant Valley
items.notableEvomon: First wild catches; the opening zone right after the tutorial portal.
items.cardSummary: The first open island after the tutorial. Wild Evomon and the boss lean Rock and Ground, so a Grass, Ground or Water starter has the early edge here.
items.verificationNote: Sportskeeda and Nerdschalk list Pebgolem (Lv 15) as the first island boss; Pro Game Guides describes Verdant Valley as the Rock/Ground starter zone.
items.imageStatus: accepted-missing: no clean reusable per-island zone art or mappable boss render found; zone-image sources (evomon.org, bo3.gg) inaccessible (403/empty), dex sources are JS catalogs of standard-creature art only. Text-first collection.

items.name: Petal Pond
items.notableEvomon: Mostly Normal-type wild Evomon; hosts the EXP challenge for fast leveling.
items.cardSummary: The second island, full of Normal-type Evomon and home to the EXP challenge area that players use to level quickly. The boss Clamspire is Water-type.
items.verificationNote: Sportskeeda/Nerdschalk: Clamspire boss (Lv 30, Water). Pro Game Guides and evomon.site note Petal Pond is Normal-type and hosts an EXP/challenge area.
items.imageStatus: accepted-missing: no clean reusable per-island zone art or mappable boss render found; zone-image sources (evomon.org, bo3.gg) inaccessible (403/empty), dex sources are JS catalogs of standard-creature art only. Text-first collection.

items.name: Lava Crag
items.notableEvomon: Fire-themed island where a Water-focused team holds a strong type advantage.
items.cardSummary: The third island and the first big difficulty step. It is Fire-themed, so a Water team dominates both the wild Evomon and the boss Empixy King.
items.verificationNote: Sportskeeda/Nerdschalk: Empixy King (Lv 45, Fire). Destructoid confirms Lava Crag is 'the third island'. Pro Game Guides confirms Fire theme and Water advantage.
items.imageStatus: accepted-missing: no clean reusable per-island zone art or mappable boss render found; zone-image sources (evomon.org, bo3.gg) inaccessible (403/empty), dex sources are JS catalogs of standard-creature art only. Text-first collection.

items.name: Amber Acres
items.notableEvomon: Grass-leaning zone where an all-Water team starts to struggle.
items.cardSummary: The fourth island, where the Grass-type wild Evomon and boss Datunymph King punish a pure Water team. Pro Game Guides suggests adding Fire coverage by this point.
items.verificationNote: Sportskeeda/Nerdschalk: Datunymph King (Lv 60, Grass). Pro Game Guides notes Grass theme and recommends Fire-type coverage here.
items.imageStatus: accepted-missing: no clean reusable per-island zone art or mappable boss render found; zone-image sources (evomon.org, bo3.gg) inaccessible (403/empty), dex sources are JS catalogs of standard-creature art only. Text-first collection.

items.name: Shiver Snows
items.cardSummary: The fifth island and the start of the mid-game. It is Ice-themed, so Fire and Rock coverage helps against the boss Glacitadel.
items.verificationNote: Sportskeeda/Nerdschalk: Glacitadel (Lv 75, Ice). This is the last island Nerdschalk flags as 'consistently confirmed in written guides'.

items.name: Raven Ridge
items.notableEvomon: Bluebird can spawn at a sky spot reached by climbing the vines around the area.
items.cardSummary: A mid-game island whose boss Volcrest King stacks attack buffs each turn, so the fight gets harder the longer it runs. A confirmed in-game zone name.
items.verificationNote: Boss name/level (Volcrest King, Lv 90) is Sportskeeda single-source. Zone name 'Raven Ridge' independently confirmed by Destructoid (Bluebird sky-spot spawn).
items.imageStatus: accepted-missing: no clean reusable per-island zone art or mappable boss render found; zone-image sources (evomon.org, bo3.gg) inaccessible (403/empty), dex sources are JS catalogs of standard-creature art only. Text-first collection.

items.name: Flying Territory
items.notableEvomon: Defeating the boss here ('King of Flying') unlocks Sundercrene as a flying mount for faster travel.
items.cardSummary: An aerial zone where beating the boss grants the Sundercrene flying mount. NOTE: 'Flying Territory' may be a descriptive label rather than the real in-game zone name and must be verified before publish.
items.verificationNote: Sportskeeda lists Sundercrene (Lv 100). Multiple sources call this the 'King of Flying' encounter that grants a flying mount, but the exact in-game ZONE NAME is unconfirmed - flagged for in-game verification per parent.

items.name: Silent Sands
items.notableEvomon: Home to the Equipment Dungeon, which unlocks around Level 40 for gear farming.
items.cardSummary: A desert island known for its Equipment Dungeon, a gear-farming activity that opens earlier (around Lv 40) than the island's boss Gearforged King.
items.verificationNote: Boss (Gearforged King, Lv 105) is Sportskeeda single-source. Pro Game Guides independently confirms Silent Sands hosts an Equipment Dungeon unlocking ~Lv 40.

items.name: Thunder Cliffs
items.notableEvomon: Thunder Cliffs boss drops Arcub; the highest-level progression island currently documented.
items.cardSummary: The final documented progression island, capped by the Level 200 King of Thunder. Its boss drops Arcub, making it a key late-game farm.
